transposeCell: Row {r}, column {c} of the transpose: it is {a} of A and equals {v}
transposeLead: The rows of A become the columns of Aᵗ: row i of A is column i of Aᵗ. Move the pointer over Aᵗ to see where each number comes from.
pairInfo: {a} = {v} sits in row {i}, column {j} of A and moves to row {j}, column {i} of Aᵗ.
pairDiagonal: {a} = {v} is on the diagonal: it stays in place when you transpose.
pairNone: Pick a number of Aᵗ to see its partner in A.
hintTypes: One matrix can be of several types at once: the identity is square, diagonal, symmetric and triangular.
whyNeedSquare: Only square matrices can be of this type, and this one has {m} rows and {n} columns.
whySquareYes: It has {m} rows and {n} columns: the same number.
whyIdentityYes: Ones on the diagonal and zeros everywhere else.
whyOffDiagonal: {a} = {v} is off the diagonal and is not 0.
whyDiagonalNotOne: {a} = {v} is on the diagonal and is not 1.
whyDiagonalYes: Every entry off the diagonal is 0.
whyAntiYes: The diagonal is 0 and every entry satisfies aᵢⱼ = −aⱼᵢ.
whyAntiDiagonal: {a} = {v} is on the diagonal and would have to be 0 (aᵢᵢ = −aᵢᵢ only holds for 0).
whyUpperYes: Every entry below the diagonal is 0.
whyUpperYesRect: Every entry below the diagonal is 0 (when it is not square it looks like an echelon matrix, but it is one only if each pivot lies to the right of the pivot in the row above).
whyBelow: {a} = {v} is below the diagonal and is not 0.
whyLowerYes: Every entry above the diagonal is 0.
whyLowerYesRect: Every entry above the diagonal is 0.
whyAbove: {a} = {v} is above the diagonal and is not 0.
splitNeedSquare: Only a square matrix splits like this. Add rows or columns until it is square.
splitOk: Checked: S + K gives exactly A, entry by entry.
splitBad: S + K does not give A.
splitHint: S is symmetric and K is antisymmetric. Every square matrix is the sum of one of each type.
